title.narrative: Project to operate the artificial limbs center in Ma'rib Governorate (Phase Ten)

description.narrative: 1. Providing physical rehabilitation services to people with special needs, following up with them and benefiting from them in serving the community. 2. Diagnosing and determining the treatment plan for each patient individually, fitting all types of limbs, providing functional rehabilitation services for prosthetic and orthotic limbs and continuous follow-up. 3. Developing the professional and scientific capabilities of the technical staff to deal with specific cases. 4. Reducing the migration of specialized medical and technical personnel. General objective: Localizing and improving prosthetic and rehabilitation services, assisting people with special needs in their integration into social life, maintaining their continued performance within the community, and raising the capabilities of workers in the Prosthetic Limbs Center with the latest medical sciences.

Operating the Prosthetic Limbs and Rehabilitation Center in Ma'rib Governorate - Republic of Yemen, by providing prosthetic limbs and physical rehabilitation for patients with motor disabilities and various types of injuries (amputation - nerve and muscle injuries). Local technical cadres are employed in the field of prosthetics manufacturing and development to cover all the needs of patients with this type of injury.

• Providing functional rehabilitation services for amputees through the manufacture and installation of 450 new limbs. • Providing physical rehabilitation through physical therapy for 3,200 beneficiaries. • Providing technical rehabilitation services for limbs through maintenance, repair, and replacement of parts for 600 limbs. • Providing medical and technical consulting services to 2,300 beneficiaries through orthopedic specialists and physical therapists contracted with the project. • Developing the scientific and professional level of the center's technical staff in the field of manufacturing and installing limbs, to keep abreast of modern scientific and academic developments. • Reducing the migration of specialized medical and technical personnel by providing 48 job opportunities for a period of 12 months.
